title: Compassion of Christ
definition: The Compassion of Christ is His holy, tender mercy toward sinners, sufferers, outcasts, and the needy.
summary: The Compassion of Christ is His holy, tender mercy toward sinners, sufferers, outcasts, and the needy.
christFocus: Jesus shows the heart of God by drawing near to the broken, touching the unclean, welcoming the rejected, and giving Himself to save the lost.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Christ's compassion is not shallow pity. It is mercy that moves toward people in need. Scripture shows Jesus seeing crowds, grieving sufferers, hungry people, diseased bodies, shamed sinners, and wandering sheep with a heart moved by love.

His compassion never ignores truth. Jesus comforts, heals, teaches, confronts sin, forgives, and calls people to follow Him. He does not use brokenness as a reason to reject people; He enters it with mercy and authority.

At the cross, compassion reaches its deepest place. The Savior who touched lepers and welcomed sinners gives His life for the helpless. His compassion is not only emotional; it is redemptive.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel unwanted by God because they have been unwanted by people. The compassion of Christ speaks directly to that wound: Jesus is not disgusted by weakness, disability, shame, recovery, grief, or failure.

This doctrine also corrects harsh religion. Truth without Christlike compassion misrepresents the Savior, while compassion without truth cannot truly heal.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring your weakness and need to Christ instead of hiding. Receive His mercy, let Him teach and restore you, and show His compassion to others who feel unseen, rejected, or too broken to be loved.
